about: Federal program access by immigration status, as of 2026-10-24. Plain-language guide, not legal advice. Values: yes | limited | no | varies. 'limited' always has a note saying who. Every row cites sources below. States can add coverage on top (see state_policy.json).

statuses.label: Refugee or asylee (no green card yet)
Work, student or visitor visa
statuses.label_es: Visa de trabajo, estudiante o visitante

programs.label: Emergency shelter, meals, food banks
programs.label_es: Albergue de emergencia, comidas, bancos de comida

*: Open to everyone. These programs generally do not ask about immigration status. A federal court vacated the 2025 notices that tried to change this (Sept 21, 2026).
Hospitals with an ER must screen and stabilize anyone, regardless of status or ability to pay (EMTALA).
Health centers serve everyone on a sliding fee. HHS's 2025 attempt to add status checks was vacated Sept 21, 2026.
Every child can enroll in public K-12 regardless of status (Plyler v. Doe). Kids without a fixed address can enroll right away (McKinney-Vento).

lpr: 5-year wait for most adults. Children under 18, people with disabilities, and green-card holders who came as refugees/asylees can get SNAP right away.
refugee_asylee: H.R. 1 (July 2025) ended SNAP for refugees and asylees until they get a green card.
survivor: Lost under H.R. 1 unless you have a green card. Some states have their own food help.
undocumented: U.S.-citizen children in the family can still get SNAP for themselves.
unsure: Depends on your exact papers. A legal aid office can check.

*: No federal immigration rule. See the public-charge row before applying if you plan to apply for a green card.

citizen: If income is low enough. In the 10 states without Medicaid expansion, most adults without kids or a disability cannot get it.
lpr: 5-year wait for most adults. Many states cover lawfully residing children and pregnant people right away.
refugee_asylee: Since Oct 1, 2026 (H.R. 1) adults lose Medicaid until they get a green card; some states still cover children and pregnant people.
asylum_pending: Not for adults. Some states cover lawfully residing children and pregnant people.
tps: Not for adults. Some states cover lawfully residing children and pregnant people.
parole: Not for adults since Oct 1, 2026. Some states cover lawfully residing children and pregnant people.
survivor: Not for adults since Oct 1, 2026 unless you have a green card. Some states cover children and pregnant people.
daca: Some states pay for coverage with state money (see your state).
undocumented: Emergency Medicaid and state-funded programs may still help (see your state).

*: Pays for emergency care, including labor and delivery, for people who meet income rules but not status rules.

programs.label: Marketplace insurance with tax credits
programs.label_es: Seguro del Mercado con créditos fiscales

asylum_pending: Lawfully present immigrants under 100% of poverty lost tax credits Jan 1, 2026; all tax credits end Jan 1, 2027 (H.R. 1).
parole: Lawfully present immigrants under 100% of poverty lost tax credits Jan 1, 2026; all tax credits end Jan 1, 2027 (H.R. 1).
survivor: Tax credits end Jan 1, 2027 unless you have a green card (H.R. 1).
visa: Some lawfully present visa holders can buy plans; check eligibility.
undocumented: Cannot buy Marketplace plans. Some states run their own programs (see your state).

asylum_pending: Mixed-status families get prorated help today; a Feb 2026 HUD proposal would end that (not final).
tps: Mixed-status families get prorated help today; a Feb 2026 HUD proposal would end that (not final).
daca: Mixed-status families get prorated help today; a Feb 2026 HUD proposal would end that (not final).
undocumented: Mixed-status families get prorated help today; a Feb 2026 HUD proposal would end that (not final).

asylum_pending: You can apply for a work permit after your case has been pending 150 days.
parole: Depends on your parole type; many need an EAD.
survivor: With an approved T/U visa or VAWA work permit.

programs.label: Could using benefits hurt a future green card?
programs.label_es: ¿Usar beneficios podría afectar una futura residencia?

lpr5: Generally does not apply once you have a green card (long trips abroad are an exception).
lpr: Generally does not apply once you have a green card (long trips abroad are an exception).
refugee_asylee: Refugees and asylees are exempt when they adjust based on that status.
survivor: T/U visa holders and VAWA self-petitioners are exempt when adjusting on that basis.
cuban_haitian: Cuban Adjustment Act applicants are exempt.
asylum_pending: A new rule (Sept 18, 2026) lets officers weigh many more benefits. Talk to a legal aid office before applying.
tps: A new rule (Sept 18, 2026) lets officers weigh many more benefits. Talk to a legal aid office before applying.
daca: A new rule (Sept 18, 2026) lets officers weigh many more benefits. Talk to a legal aid office before applying.
parole: A new rule (Sept 18, 2026) lets officers weigh many more benefits. Talk to a legal aid office before applying.
visa: A new rule (Sept 18, 2026) lets officers weigh many more benefits. Talk to a legal aid office before applying.
undocumented: If you might apply for a green card later, talk to a legal aid office before applying for benefits.
unsure: Talk to a legal aid office before applying for benefits.
